quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Google, in its Site Reliability Engineering book, describes SRE as what happens when you ask a software engineer to design an operations team: its SRE teams hire software engineers to run products and to build systems that do work otherwise done, often manually, by system administrators.

quick_facts.label: What an SRE team looks after
quick_facts.value: Google says an SRE team is responsible for the availability, latency, performance, efficiency, change management, monitoring, emergency response and capacity planning of its services.

quick_facts.label: Half the time is engineering
quick_facts.value: Google places a 50% cap on the aggregate operations work (tickets, on-call and manual tasks) for all its SREs; the remaining time is meant for development.

sections.heading: What a site reliability engineer does
paragraphs: Site reliability engineering began at Google. Its SRE book describes the job as running large services with a software engineer's approach: instead of doing operations work by hand, SREs write software and build systems that do it.
The description below is Google's own account of its SRE teams. Other companies use the same title for similar work, and the details differ between them.
bullets: Keep services available and fast: availability, latency, performance and efficiency.
Manage change, since Google reports that roughly 70% of outages are due to changes in a live system.
Monitor services and respond to emergencies, including being on call.
Plan capacity so the service can keep up with demand.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: Google describes its SRE teams as 50–60% Google software engineers, with the rest being candidates very close to its software engineering qualifications who bring other skills, such as UNIX system internals and networking.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering; Software Developer.
Less common routes on the map: Systems Administrator.
